explanation: The structure that surrounds and protects Jerusalem, which Nehemiah was commissioned to rebuild.
The process of repairing and restoring something that has been destroyed or damaged, such as the wall around Jerusalem in the book of Nehemiah.
A Jewish leader and governor who helped rebuild the wall around Jerusalem after the exile in Babylon.
The holy city for the Jews and the capital of Israel; the center of Jewish faith and culture.
The period when the Jews were forced to leave their homeland and live in Babylon.
The ancient kingdom and city where the Jews were held in exile before returning to Jerusalem to rebuild the city and its walls.
The entrances to the city of Jerusalem that were part of the wall and had to be rebuilt along with the wall itself.
The volunteers who helped Nehemiah rebuild the wall and the city gates around Jerusalem.
Religious leaders within Judaism who also participated in the work of rebuilding the wall.
